nodes.title: Read the fields the API actually returns

anchor.snippet: setSearch({ status: 'success', items: data.items, total: data.total });

nodes.why: The API resolves { items, total }. The starter read data.results, and the any annotation hid the mismatch, so every search looked empty.
nodes.alternative: Keep any and add data.results ?? data.items as a fallback.
nodes.tradeoff: Typing the callback as SearchResponse lets the compiler catch the next shape change instead of the user.

nodes.title: Model the search as one status union
nodes.why: Loading, success with items and total, and error with a message can never overlap, so the page cannot show rows and an error at once.
nodes.alternative: Keep results, loading and error as three separate states.
nodes.tradeoff: A union costs one type up front and removes every impossible combination from the render.

nodes.title: Search again whenever the query changes
nodes.why: With an empty dependency array the effect ran only on mount, so typing never triggered a new search.
nodes.alternative: Call searchProducts from the onChange handler.
nodes.tradeoff: The effect keeps one code path for the first search and every later one.

nodes.title: Reset to loading at the start of every search
nodes.why: Old rows and old errors disappear immediately, so the user never reads results for a query they already changed.
nodes.alternative: Keep the previous results visible while the next search runs.
nodes.tradeoff: Clearing is simpler and honest; keeping stale rows needs an explicit stale label.

nodes.title: Ignore responses from an older query
nodes.why: A one-letter query answers after a longer one, so without the guard the older response overwrote the newer results.
nodes.tradeoff: Debouncing reduces requests but cannot stop a slow network from reordering them; the guard can.

nodes.title: Turn a rejection into an error state
nodes.why: Without a catch the promise rejection left the loading line on screen forever and logged an unhandled rejection.
nodes.alternative: Wrap the call in try and catch inside an async function.
nodes.tradeoff: Both work; the catch keeps the same cancelled check as the success path.

nodes.title: Read the count from the total the API returns
nodes.why: The page shows at most five items, so only total can say how many products match.
nodes.tradeoff: Counting rows would always print five for broad queries; total is the real number.

nodes.title: Show the empty state only after a search returns nothing
nodes.why: The starter showed the empty message whenever the list was empty, including during loading and after the wrong-field bug.
nodes.alternative: Show the empty message whenever there are no rows.
nodes.tradeoff: Tying it to a finished search with total 0 keeps the message truthful.
